mcqs.learning_point: Understand blocks of the periodic table
mcqs.question: Which of the following comparisons between s‑block and d‑block elements is correct?

options.A: s‑block elements typically exhibit only one oxidation state, whereas d‑block elements exhibit a wide range of oxidation states.
options.B: s‑block elements have their valence electrons in ns orbitals, while d‑block elements have their valence electrons in (n‑1)d orbitals.
options.C: s‑block elements are located on the right side of the periodic table, whereas d‑block elements are on the left side.
options.D: s‑block elements have higher electronegativity than d‑block elements.

mcqs.answer: s‑block elements have their valence electrons in ns orbitals, while d‑block elements have their valence electrons in (n‑1)d orbitals.
mcqs.explanation: In the periodic table, s‑block elements have their outermost electrons in the ns subshell (e.g., 1s, 2s, 3s). d‑block elements have their valence electrons in the (n‑1)d subshell, such as 3d for period 4 elements. Option B correctly states this distinction. Options A, C and D contain inaccurate statements about oxidation states, position, and electronegativity.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate electronic configuration to periodic position
mcqs.question: The element with electron configuration [Ar] 4s² 3d¹⁰ 4p² belongs to which group and period in the periodic table?
mcqs.explanation: The configuration ends with 4p², indicating the element is in the p‑block of the fourth period. The p‑block groups start from Group 13; adding two electrons (p²) places the element in Group 14. Hence the element is in Group 14, Period 4 (it is carbon‑group element, silicon). The other options either give wrong group numbers or wrong periods.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly states the modern periodic law?

options.A: The physical and chemical properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses.
options.B: The physical and chemical properties of elements repeat periodically with increasing atomic number.
options.C: Elements in the same period have identical chemical properties.
options.D: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of neutrons in its nucleus.

mcqs.answer: The physical and chemical properties of elements repeat periodically with increasing atomic number.
mcqs.explanation: Mendeleev’s original law used atomic mass, but the modern periodic law, established after the discovery of the proton, states that properties are periodic functions of atomic number (Z). Option B captures this. Option A reflects the outdated version, C is false because elements in a period show varying properties, and D confuses protons with neutrons.

mcqs.question: Why is the atomic number considered the fundamental basis for arranging elements in the periodic table?

options.A: Because atomic number equals the number of protons, which determines the nuclear charge and electron configuration.
options.B: Because atomic number is the same as atomic mass for all elements.
options.C: Because atomic number indicates the number of neutrons, which defines chemical behavior.
options.D: Because atomic number is directly proportional to the element’s density.

mcqs.answer: Because atomic number equals the number of protons, which determines the nuclear charge and electron configuration.
mcqs.explanation: The atomic number (Z) is the count of protons in the nucleus. It sets the positive charge that attracts electrons, thereby fixing the electron configuration and chemical properties. Hence Z is the logical ordering parameter. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: In the periodic table, a "period" and a "group" are defined as:

options.A: A period is a vertical column; a group is a horizontal row.
options.B: A period is a horizontal row; a group is a vertical column.
options.C: Both period and group refer to vertical columns.
options.D: Both period and group refer to horizontal rows.

mcqs.answer: A period is a horizontal row; a group is a vertical column.
mcqs.explanation: Periods run left to right across the table (rows) and indicate the principal quantum number. Groups run top to bottom (columns) and contain elements with similar valence electron configurations. Option B correctly captures this; the other options invert or duplicate the definitions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand blocks of the periodic table
mcqs.question: An element whose outermost electrons occupy the 3d subshell would be classified in which block of the periodic table?
mcqs.explanation: The d‑block consists of elements whose differentiating (or valence) electrons enter (n‑1)d orbitals. If the highest‑energy electrons are in 3d, the element belongs to the d‑block (transition metals). The s‑, p‑, and f‑blocks involve ns, np, and (n‑2)f electrons respectively.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate electronic configuration to periodic position
mcqs.question: Given the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 3d¹⁰ 4p⁵, the element is most likely to be found in which group and period?
mcqs.explanation: The configuration ends with 4p⁵, indicating a p‑block element in the fourth period. The p⁵ configuration corresponds to the halogen group, which is Group 17. Therefore the element (bromine) is in Group 17, Period 4. The other options mismatch either the group or the period.

mcqs.question: A newly synthesized element has atomic number 119. According to the modern periodic law, which of the following statements is most plausible regarding its chemical behavior?

options.A: It will behave similarly to the alkali metals of group 1.
options.B: It will behave similarly to the noble gases of group 18.
options.C: It will behave similarly to the transition metals of the d‑block.
options.D: It will behave similarly to the halogens of group 17.

mcqs.answer: It will behave similarly to the alkali metals of group 1.
mcqs.explanation: Element 119 would be placed in the first group of the seventh period, extending the alkali metal family. The modern periodic law predicts that elements in the same group exhibit similar chemical properties because they have analogous valence electron configurations (ns¹). Hence option A is correct. Options B, C, and D refer to groups that are not aligned with the position of element 119.
